articleTitle: Non-destructive testing of glass fibre reinforced plastics with a synthetic aperture radar in the lower THz region
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The non-destructive testing (NDT) of glass fibre reinforced plastics (GFRP) becomes more and more important. A test setup using a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) at frequencies of 220 - 325 GHz was set up to detect artificial defects in the probe. The paper will present experimental results and will furthermore address the challenges of imaging GFRP samples in a reflection geometry setup.

articleTitle: 0.14THz high speed data communication over 1.5 kilometers
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A 0.14THz point to point communication system based on all solid-state electronic devices has been developed. The carrier frequency is 140.3GHz with output power of -1dBm. 16 QAM modulation has been applied in signal processing to achieve 2.75 bit/Hz spectrum efficiency. It has successfully transmitted 10Gbit/s data over 1.5km with bit error rate (BER)<;1e-6 based on non-realtime software demodulation. 2Gbit/s data transmission has also been realized over 1.5km with BER=1.7e-7 based on realtime hardware demodulation.

articleTitle: On the co-design between on-chip antennas and THz MOSFET direct detectors in CMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This paper reports on co-design between CMOS direct detectors and silicon lens-integrated on-chip antennas. Due the appropriate impedance characteristics of the differentially driven antenna, broadband detector operation over multiple hundred GHz centered around 900 GHz could be achieved. The overall pixel layout is fully compatible with an industry qualified CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Terahertz imaging through paint layers
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz spectroscopic imaging through paint layers as a method of nondestructive inspection has been studied in a wide frequency range from 0.1 to 100 THz. As paint layers actual use multilayer coatings were examined. This method has also been demonstrated for the imaging of an invisible rusty area covered with multiple paint layers on a steel using a specified frequency of THz range.

articleTitle: Capacity analysis for high-speed terahertz wireless communications
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on the analytical capacity analysis of terahertz wireless communications supporting 275–325 GHz frequency band. Our goal in this paper is to provide design guidelines for close proximity links with transmission capacity beyond 100 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Ultrafast high-resolution THz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Ultrafast time-domain spectroscopy based on free induction decay radiation of molecules excited by NovoFEL THz pulses is described. The radiation was detected by ultrafast Schottky diode detectors with a rise time shorter than 20 ps. The highest spectral resolution of the method is limited by the lowest repetition frequency of NovoFEL pulses, which constitutes 5.6 MHz. Routine spectral measurements can be made for a time of one nanosecond. The technique can be used to study ultrafast nonrepeatable phenomena. Another application is a spectral “cinema” with a picture frequency of up to 22.5 MHz.

articleTitle: Diffraction measurements at 60 GHz and 300 GHz for modeling of future THz communication systems
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Indoor wireless communication channels will be operated in the 60 GHz band soon and will work at 300 GHz and beyond in the foreseeable future. Although diffraction occurs at a multitude of objects in indoor environments and needs to be considered for reliable propagation simulations, very few work exists on this topic in the mm and sub-mm wave bands. Here, we present measurements of the diffraction at wedges (cuboids) at 300 GHz with different materials and real antennas. The measurements are used to validate theoretic descriptions of diffraction phenomena.

articleTitle: Terahertz frequency agility of uncooled antenna-coupled microbolometer arrays
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Antenna coupled bolometers developed at CEA-Leti can address the whole THz range by proper tailoring of the antennas while keeping the technological stack unchanged. This paper presents the flexibility of the design regarding absorption frequency and presents its capability to sense frequencies below 1 THz.

articleTitle: Schottky diode arrays for submillimeter-wave sideband generation
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A 100-element varactor sideband generator array for operation at 1.6 THz has been designed and fabricated. The array consists of varactor Schottky diodes fabricated on GaAs and integrated into an array of bowtie antennas. An integrated transmission line stub is included to tune the diode parasitic capacitance. Harmonic balance simulations predict the array to have a sideband conversion loss of 8.3 dB.

articleTitle: Detailed observation of modulation instability on THz NovoFEL
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Detailed experimental observations of the modulation instability in the frequency and time domains were made on the THz NovoFEL by a Fourier spectrometer and an ultrafast Schottky diode detector. The regime stabilized by negative detuning between the electron and light frequencies is shown to transform into a multimode one with coherent modulation of the light pulse. Further decrease in the stabilization factor leads, for a high gain, to an unstable regime at the resonance frequency. In this regime, a light pulse splits into incoherent sub-pulses with a duration equal to the slippage length divided by the light velocity. The generation of one short sub-pulse is possible for small positive detuning.

articleTitle: Measurements of paint thickness of automobiles by using THz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: THz time-domain spectroscopy was applied to the thickness measurements of multi-layer paint of automobiles. The thickness of three layers could be estimated from the waveforms and the values showed good agreement with those obtained by electromagnetic thickness tester. Drying processes after coating were possibly monitored.

articleTitle: Chemometric tools for analysing Terahertz fingerprints in a postscanner
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Concerning several attacks using letter bombs within Europe in the last couple of years and the highly rising number of new drugs, there is a need for new kinds of detection devices for explosives and drugs. We present a postscanner on basis of Terahertz (THz) spectroscopy using novel chemometric methods for the evaluation of detected THz fingerprints.

articleTitle: Development of a compact sub-terahertz gyrotron and its application to t-ray real-time imaging for food inspection
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A sub-terahertz gyrotron, employed with a compact cryogen-free magnet, is developed to be used as an illumination source of the active T-ray imaging system for food inspection in real time. Details of the gyrotron development, as well as some preliminary results of real-time T-ray imaging of foreign bodies hidden in food, will be presented.

articleTitle: THz technology applied to cultural heritage
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz (THz) spectroscopy and imaging techniques have great potential as analytical tools in the field of heritage science. The advantages of THz technology, such as nondestructive spectroscopic imaging and tomography, are introduced including case studies of historic masterpieces.

articleTitle: Development of a table-top 200 GHz gyrotron FU CW CII with an internal mode convertor
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A table-top gyrotron with an internal mode convertor was designed and fabricated at FIR FU. The length of the gyrotron is as small as 860 mm. The output power higher than 1 kW at 203.4 GHz is expected. The oscillation of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3,3</sub> mode was confirmed in an initial test operation.

articleTitle: Exceptional tunability of THz reflectance in graphene structures
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a graphene-based device achieving extraordinary control of terahertz (THz) wave reflectance. The advantages of graphene based switchable THz devices include low cost, facile fabrication and excellent tunability, thus promising for THz system applications.

articleTitle: Progress of high power multi-frequency gyrotron development
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The multi-frequency gyrotron are under development in JAEA. Oscillations at 170 GHz, 137 GHz and 104 GHz are demonstrated with the Gaussian beam output. At present, 0.9 MW/70 sec, 1.1 MW/5 sec were obtained at 170 GHz. In parallel, a fast frequency control was demonstrated between 170 GHz and 167 GHz using a super-conducting sweeping coil.

articleTitle: Design of multi-order diffractive THz lenses
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Quadratic, multi-order diffractive lenses have been designed, fabricated, and demonstrated for the MMW-THz region, with the capability of focusing harmonic wavelengths on to a common focal point. Design wavelength and harmonic spacing can be chosen as design parameters, allowing great flexibility in lens design. Simulations were carried out to determine lens parameters and performance. These lenses reduce both spherical and chromatic aberrations at harmonic wavelengths, and are thinner and lighter than traditional refractive elements. This lens type is potentially useful to sensor fusion architectures.

articleTitle: Addressing the temperature stability in an 89 GHz Schottky detector design for radiometry
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A detector design for the 89 GHz channel of direct detection radiometers is proposed with high sensitive zerobias Schottky diodes. Particularly addressed is the diode's RF voltage responsivity drift with temperature at millimeter wave frequencies between 60 and 200 GHz, as well as its compensation in the microstrip circuit.

articleTitle: Continuous-wave terahertz near-field spectroscopy and imaging with a micro-machined photomixer probe-tip
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Using a photomixer-equipped probe-tip and a fiber-coupled two-color diode laser, optoelectronic coherent terahertz near-field measurements are reported in the frequency-domain for the first time. The system is successfully applied to spatial and spectral investigations of resonant metamaterial structures.

articleTitle: Material characterization at low frequencies using THz and Raman spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present results from wideband THz, low wave-number Raman, and FTIR measurements on benzoic acid and two of its derivatives. The low energy vibrational modes have been identified and compared with the results from calculations.

articleTitle: Development of a continuously frequency tunable gyrotron operating at the fundamental resonance for 600 MHz DNP-NMR spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Continuously frequency tunable gyrotron, FU CW VIB, which is of sealed-off type has been developed for 600 MHz DNP-NMR at FIR FU. The frequency tuning bandwidth reached 1.4 GHz. The output power was ranged from 15 to 130 W.

articleTitle: Nanogrid-based vertically integrated photomixer for continuous wave terahertz generation
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This work proposes a new type of continuous-wave (CW) terahertz (THz) generation based on vertically integrated LTG-GaAs photomixer and Nanogrid-based transparent top bias-electrode. The THz output power can be increased by higher available photocurrents and smaller device capacitances. A suitable resonant antenna design is proposed.

articleTitle: Terahertz technology for the detection of food contaminants
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this paper, an application of terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) to detection of food contaminants is introduced. Spectra of chemical food contaminants, carbendazim, chlorothalonil, and isoprothiolane were measured and analyzed by THz-TDS in frequency from 0.2 - 3.5 THz.

articleTitle: 2 MW Coaxial-Cavity Pre-Prototype Gyrotron for ITER - recent experiments with the modified gyrotron setup -
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A 2 MW, CW, 170 GHz coaxial-cavity gyrotron for electron cyclotron heating and current drive in the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) is under development within the European Gyrotron Consortium (EGYC). To support the development of the industrial CW prototype, studies on a short pulse tube, similar to the industrial gyrotron, are performed in parallel at KIT. Significant design modifications have been performed on the pre-prototype, recently. The results of the ongoing experiments are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Carbon nanotube based prototype as THz time domain sources/detectors
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Photoconductive switches have been extensively studied in time domain spectroscopy (TDS) as THz sources/ detectors. The commonly used devices consist of metal-semiconductor-metal (MSM) structure where Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) is the active layer. In this work, an approach consisting of using semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes (s-SWCNTs) instead is proposed. The pristine results showing the photo-response of CNT is presented to illustrate our purpose.

articleTitle: Polarization sensitive millimeter-wave imaging sensor based on optical up-conversion scaled to a distributed aperture
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A polarization sensitive millimeter-wave sensor operating at 77 GHz is built and characterized. The sensor is scalable to a distributed aperture architecture and results are presented from using multiple antennas. Imagery is also presented from a 30-element distributed aperture system that is only sensitive to one polarization.

articleTitle: Cross-polarization in quasi-optical receivers: ALMA band 4 and 10
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A careful study about the influence of individual optical components on receiver cross-polarization has been performed. The basic mechanisms of generation of cross-polarization in ellipsoidal mirrors and dielectrics have been reviewed and characterized in terms of higher-order Gaussian beam modes. A simple model considering the phase differences of different Gaussian beam modes is proposed in order to calculate the final system cross-polarization pattern. This model has been successfully used to characterize the total cross-polarization in two cryogenically-cooled receivers for astronomy: ALMA band 4 and band 10.

articleTitle: Curvature control of silicon microlens for THz dielectric antenna
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have controlled the curvature of silicon microlens by changing the amount of photoresist in order to microfabricate hemispherical silicon microlens which can improve the directivity and reduce substrate mode losses.

articleTitle: Vibrational spectra of nylon-6, nylon-6/6, nylom-11 and nylon-12 studied by terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz absorption spectra were measured for nylon-6/6, nylon-6, nylon-11 and nylon-12 by Fourier transform far-infrared spectroscopy. Different spectral features among the four species were interpreted as the characteristics of crystalline conformations of nylons.

articleTitle: High frequency performance of GaAsSb/InAlAs/InGaAs tunnel diodes at 220 GHz
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We evaluated performance of zero-bias, square-law GaAsSb/InAlAs/InGaAs tunnel diodes at frequencies up to 220 GHz. The detectors with submicron cross-sectional area demonstrated sensitivities above 500 V/W, and curvature coefficients of 20 V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of a broadband calorimeter for mm-wave power standard in the frequency range from 110 GHz to 170 GHz
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A broadband rectangular waveguide calorimeter was designed to establish a reliable mm-wave power standard in the frequency range from 110 GHz to 170 GHz. This calorimeter precisely measures the absorbed mm-wave power in the mm-wave absorber by comparison with the equivalent DC power, which ensures the SI traceability of the measured mm-wave power.

articleTitle: Terahertz transmission spectra of composite materials based on MWNT with different time of ultrasonic processing
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The electromagnetic response properties of PMMA based composites containing multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWNT) produced using different time of ultrasonic treatment are investigated in the terahertz frequency range.

articleTitle: Stabilization of gyrotron output power using feedback control
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Beam current of gyrotron was stabilized from 17 % to 0.5% by the feedback control to adjust the heater voltage of electron gun. The fluctuation level of output power was decreased from 15 % to 5 %. More effective stabilization of the output power up to 2% was attained by feedback control to adjust heater voltage.

articleTitle: Stability of signals generated with a dual-frequency laser and a UTC photodiode up to 700 GHz
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Low phase noise and tunable THz-signals from 300 GHz to 1 THz are obtained with a combination of a unitravelling carrier photodiode and a solid-state dual-frequency laser at 1.5 μm. The spectral purity is precisely characterized. Phase noises as low as -20 dBc/Hz at 1 kHz offset from the carrier frequency and an Allan deviation of 3·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> on 100 s are obtained.

articleTitle: Integrated continuous-wave THz control unit with 1 THz tuning range
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: An integrated photonic chip allows for full control of the THz signal in cw THz photomixing systems. This THz control unit does provide direct access to the THz amplitude and phase via standard electronics as well as continuous tuning of the beat frequency over a frequency range larger than 1 THz.

articleTitle: Automodulation processes in THz resonant backward wave oscillator with low focusing magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The automodulation processes in THz resonant backward wave oscillator (BWO) operating at low focusing magnetic field have been studied. Automodulation behavior has been analyzed for different electron beam inclination angles. It has been shown that at low magnetic field the RF transverse electric field leads to steep change of beam-wave interaction power that causes automodulation. The theoretical results are compared with particle-in-cell simulations.

articleTitle: Cryogenic amplifier based receivers at submillimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The operating frequency of InP high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) based amplifiers has moved well in the submillimeter-wave frequencies over the last couple of years. Working amplifiers with usable gain in waveguide packages has been reported beyond 700 GHz. When cooled cryogenically, they have shown substantial improvement in their noise temperature. This has opened up the real possibility of cryogenic amplifier based heterodyne receivers at submillimeter wavelengths for ground-based, air-borne, and space-based instruments for astrophysics, planetary, and Earth science applications. This paper provides an overview of the science applications at submillimeter wavelengths that will benefit from this technology. It also describes the current state of the InP HEMT based cryogenic amplifier receivers at submillimeter wavelengths.

articleTitle: Measurement of frequency conversion losses with 3-mixer method for traceable mm-wave power measurement method in D-band
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Power measurement standard above 110 GHz is undefined even if we want to measure the power of an electromagnetic wave at the frequency. To measure the wave by using a spectrum analyzer, an external mixer was needed. In this paper, we determine the conversion losses of a mixer used with a spectrum analyzer to measure power at mm-wave frequencies. We determine the mixer conversion losses by a 3-mixer method that is based on different combinations of the 3 mixers. We then evaluate the measurement uncertainty.

articleTitle: Millimetre wave band unbiased harmonic transponder
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Harmonic transponders used nowadays for tracking small insects impede and obstruct their movements due to their large size and weight. The paper presents millimetre wave band unbiased harmonic transponder. It comprises of separate transmit and receive microstrip patch antennas and unbiased Schottky diode doubler. The transponder is conformal, miniaturized and suitable for short range insect tracking.

articleTitle: Non-invasive detection of mycobacterium tuberculosis using IR and NIR spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is a tropical disease affecting millions of lives. Conventional chemical based methods such as acid-fast technique for the detection of TB are time consuming and suffer from low sensitivity and specificity. We present a non-invasive detection technique for TB using IR and NIR spectroscopy. Spectral fingerprints of Mycobacterium are compared with E-Coli, Smegmatis and BCG bacteria. Principal component analysis on the spectral data shows that the bacteria can be distinguished easily due to their slightly different composition of cellular constituents. Non-invasive method presented here provides an attractive pathway for low cost, rapid portable diagnostic systems for TB and other diseases.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of the FR-4 substrates in the THz frequency range
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The paper describes the method of modelling a microstrip transmission line fabricated on FR-4 substrate in the GHz frequency range. The model is based on the real part of high frequency complex electric permittivity of the dielectric measured with THz time domain spectrometer. The microstrip measurement results are used to analyse the model accuracy.

articleTitle: Progress on 140 GHz, 1 MW, CW series gyrotrons for W7-X
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The construction of the 140 GHz, 1 MW CW gyrotrons for the 10 MW ECRH system of the stellarator W7-X at IPP Greifswald is ongoing. While acceptance testing of the gyrotrons is progressing, reliable output parameters and stable production have been achieved. This report summarizes the actual status and some topical results. Focus is put on the final construction and latest parameters measured at factory-acceptance tests and site-acceptance tests. Parallel to the design optimization a new spectral measurement method has been developed, which allows time-dependent broadband spectral measurements with µs resolution for ms range pulses. Results of measurements done with W7-X gyrotrons are shown.

articleTitle: A dielectric probe for near-field millimeter-wave imaging
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A dielectric probe for performing near-field imaging in the millimeter-wave band is presented. The probe consists of a rectangular slab of low-loss dielectric material which is metalized on two sides and sharpened to a point of approximately 20 μm. This structure forms a parallel-plate waveguide which offers broadband operation and strong field enhancement and localization at the tip with a spatial resolutions of λ/250. A method of exciting the probe using a metal rectangular cavity resonator is also described.

articleTitle: Investigation of spectral properties of textile
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In order to develop a Terahertz (THz) video-camera for human security scanning we investigated the spectroscopic properties of different textile materials. THz time domain spectroscopy (TDS) measurements were performed.

articleTitle: Orientation sensitive Terahertz resonances observed in protein crystals
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A method is presented for measuring anisotropic THz response for small crystals, Crystal Anisotropy Terahertz Microscopy (CATM). Sucrose CATM measurements find the expected anisotropic phonon resonances. CATM measurements of protein crystals find the expected broadband water absorption is suppressed and strong orientation and hydration dependent resonant features.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of terahertz reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this work, a reflectarray operating at 1 THz is designed and implemented using metal-dielectric resonant patch elements. The dimensions of the single elements are optimized through simulation to achieve a wide range of the reflection phase change. Based on the relation between the phase change and the patch size, the terahertz reflectarray is built up to function as a reflector deflecting an incident beam at a predesigned angle off the specular direction. In order to verify the design, a prototype is fabricated and the measurement results show that about 80% of the incident amplitude can be deflected into the desired direction around the operation frequency. The work presents an attractive concept for developing components able to efficiently manipulate terahertz radiation.

articleTitle: Identification of cellulosic fiber by terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Absorption spectra of constituents of fibers are distinguishable by THz spectroscopy, even for fibers in the same category or species. The advantage of this technique is its sensitivity to the structural differences of the fibers, even if they consist largely of the same components. The THz spectra of cellulosic fibers in the category of plant-derived fibers and regenerated cellulose fibers showed an identifiable character, as an example.

articleTitle: Medical application of THz imaging technique
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present the medical applications of the terahertz spectroscopic imaging technology to the brain and blood system as well as to the molecular imaging for the target specific imaging.

articleTitle: Development of a high-power 295 GHz fundamental-harmonic gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A high-power gyrotron is developed for use in the collective Thomson scattering diagnostic of fusion plasma. It operates at fundamental harmonic with a frequency of 295 GHz. An electron gun with an intense laminar electron beam is designed, and the oscillation power of more than 200 kW is expected.

articleTitle: Experimental results on a modular gyrotron operating at 0.26THz for 400MHz DNP/NMR spectroscopy applications
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A detailed experimental study of the operational capability of a prototype modular-gyrotron for 400MHz DNP/NMR spectroscopy is presented. Results show that the tube matches the specifications in term of nominal power, tunability, frequency purity and stability. In a different range of operating parameters, non-stationary operating regimes are observed.

articleTitle: Comparison of competing designs for delay-short calibration standards at WR-1.5
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Two competing delay-short calibration standard designs for WM-380/WR-1.5 rectangular waveguide (500-750GHz) are evaluated. Quantitative estimates of the connector uncertainty are made and it is shown that an end-milled design out-performs the shim design. The effect of each standard's repeatability on calibration uncertainty is used to determine corrected measurement uncertainty for an eighth wavelength verification standard.

articleTitle: Millimetre wave band microstrip patch antennas for harmonic transponders
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The paper describes millimetre wave band (38.5GHz and 77GHz) square microstrip patch antennas for harmonic transponders. These conformal, miniaturized and high gain antennas with symmetrical broadside patterns would allow the development of transponders with the fewest adverse effects on insects behaviours, as well as offering easy fixation and relatively high gain.

articleTitle: Complete THz system for reflection real-time imaging with uncooled antenna-coupled bolometer arrays
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: CEA-Leti has developed a real-time reflection imaging system: it combines illumination by QCL sources and a telescope that focuses the reflected radiation onto a camera that houses an uncooled 320×240 antenna-coupled micro-bolometer array driven by a FPGA card. We present first high resolution images of illuminated surfaces acquired in real-time.

articleTitle: Absorption spectra of hydrogen chloride and carbon monoxide in smoke
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Absorption spectra of smoke produced from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and molded charcoal at high temperature are investigated between 500 and 950 GHz. Observed peaks at 626 GHz for PVC and at 692 and 921 GHz for molded charcoal are respectively assigned as the spectral signature of hydrogen chloride and carbon monoxide contained in smoke. Smoke from molded charcoal also showed absorption peaks of hydrogen cyanide that are likely produced by the combustion of adhesive matter in it. These results show the potential of sub-terahertz spectroscopic sensing for instantaneous detection and quantification of multiple harmful gaseous substances in smoke.

articleTitle: Study of surface plasmons travelling along straight and curved metal-dielectric interfaces: Experiment and theory
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Terahertz surface plasmons (SPs) produced by monochromatic radiation of Novosibirsk free electron laser and travelling along straight and curved metal-dielectric interfaces have been studied experimentally. Characteristics of SPs and radiation decoupled into free space were examined with three complementary terahertz sensors (a Goley cell, a 320×240 uncooled microbolometer matrix, and a cryogenic hot electron bolometer). The terahertz electromagnetic field which arises when an SP reaches the end face of a metal slab was studied theoretically using the Sommerfeld-Malyuzhinets technique. The theoretical and experimental results are in a good agreement.

articleTitle: Generation of a wide range and stable THz wave using an optical fiber and a laser chaos
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Generation of a wide-range THz wave from a photoconductive antenna excited by a multimode semiconductor chaotic oscillation laser with an optical delayed feedback using an external mirror is investigated. An optical fiber is also used for easy alignment. The properties of the generated THz wave are compared with those of generated THz wave by using a CW steady state laser.

articleTitle: Reduction of surface losses of CVD diamond by passivation methods
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The high-power long pulse RF loss properties of CVD diamond windows for ECR heating and plasma stabilization in large fusion devices have been measured by established Fabry-Perot methods [1,2,3]. The dielectric loss is strongly influenced by the surface chemistry of the diamond. Special surface passivation techniques are investigated due to the reduction of the electrical surface conductivity and therefore of the RF losses.

articleTitle: Millimeter waves for moisture testing and treatment culture objects
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Millimeter waves as a tool for non- destructive moisture monitoring and disinfestations of artworks are introduced. Non-destructive and non invasive techniques are often irreplaceable in order to preserve and to restore cultural objects. Environmental parameters, first of all moisture, can damage culture heritage objects and also results in spring up variety of pests and other micro-organisms. Non-destructive monitoring of these damage and also disinfestation treatments and drying with help of electromagnetic waves are preferred as they keep the object untouched after treatment. Here we discuss application of millimeter waves for solving this problem. Millimeter waves have high spatial resolution and absorption in water as well as in bio-objects that are usually moist and at the same time minimal interaction with dry culture objects.

articleTitle: Military application of non-destructive properities of THz radiation
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on analysis of military-oriented composite materials by means of THz Time Domain Spectroscopy (TDS) technique in reflection configuration. The composites were hit by a bullet from a rifle and the puncture region was non-destructively imaged. We could observed delaminated and distorted layers inside the sample up to 5mm in depth.

articleTitle: Experimental and theoretical studies of mesas of several geometries for terahertz wave radiation from the intrinsic Josephson junctions in superconducting Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on intense, tunable, continuous, and coherent THz electromagnetic waves observed from differently shaped triangular mesas of the intrinsic Josephson junctions in single crystalline high-T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> superconducting Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CaCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8+δ</inf>. All samples are fabricated by focused ion beam milling.

articleTitle: Assignment of low-frequency vibrational modes of coumarin-3-carboxylic acid
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Low-frequency spectra of non-isotopic/deuterated coumarin-3-carboxylic acid under 200 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> was obtained by terahertz (THz) spectroscopy and was compared with calculated harmonic frequencies from DFT calculation with periodic systems to reveal mode assignment of the molecule in THz region.

articleTitle: Nondestructive evaluation of glued joints in nonmetallic samples using THz waves
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The quality of glued joints in nonmetallic samples was evaluated using a standard THz-TDS system in the transmission configuration. Our results show that THz waves can indeed become a powerful tool for NDE of nonmetallic industrial equipment.

articleTitle: The diffraction radiation of sub-wavelength holes array with dielectric medium loading
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In the paper we show that under the excitation of a line current, a dielectric medium loading in the lower half-space of the sub-wavelength holes array brings surprising changes to the diffraction radiation. In the lower half-space, the surface wave becomes a radiation wave. The fundamental space harmonic is transformed into Cherenkov radiation with unique characteristics and the first negative space harmonic is converted into a radiation wave with the angle of Smith-Purcell radiation. Consequently, in the lower half-space interference happens due to these two kinds of diffraction radiation.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of powerful 0.67 THz gyrotron with a pulsed solenoid for remote detection of concealed radioactive materials
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Design and results of experimental tests of a high-power sub-terahertz gyrotron with a pulse solenoid for remote detection of radioactive materials are presented. Operating frequency corresponds to the atmospheric transparency window (0.66-0.67 THz). The 200 kW output power in pulses up to 30 microsecond duration were obtained.

articleTitle: Grain growth in submillimeter wave sintered alumina
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The sub-millimeter (300 GHz) wave sintering of the alumina ceramics had been performed. Temperature dependences of the grain size and its distribution were obtained. Temperature dependence of standard deviation (STD) of the grain size distribution is different from conventional heated one (thermal equilibrium process).

articleTitle: Gate-voltage tunable terahertz detection by a GaAs/AlGaAs quantum device
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report a gate-voltage-controlled terahertz (THz) detector based on a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) field-effect transistor. The electron density of the 2DEG can be varied with the gate voltage. In this way, we controlled the amplitude of the THz detected signal by the gate voltage, indicating the role of the external switch for the THz detection.

articleTitle: Active Terahertz near-field probes for high-resolution free-carrier density imaging applications
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: First photo-conductive near-field probes combining THz generation, detection, transmission and resonant focusing element in a single micro-structured cantilever device are presented and applied to free-carrier density imaging applications in semiconductor (solar) material analytics.

articleTitle: Spectroscopy and terahertz imaging for sigillography applications
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This study focuses on the seals of validation, sealing written documents, used in the Western Middle Ages, especially wax seals. We use THz spectroscopy and imaging for non-destructive evaluation of natural materials within those seals. Using a time domain THz spectroscopy and imaging system, THz transmission images are generated in the 0.1-3 THz range and demonstrate that the spectral properties of these materials allow to see across and under a thick layer of old wax.

articleTitle: Superlattice devices applications in THz frequency range
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The results of the planar diodes based on semiconductor quantum superlattice (SL) applications for direct and coherent detection, harmonics generation in terahertz frequency range is presented. The study used planar diodes with small active area size 1-2 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. To fabricate the diodes were grown by molecular beam epitaxy structure heavily doped superlattices with miniband width 24meV. The experimental dependence of Volt -Watt sensitivity unbiased or biased planar SL diodes in frequency range 1-4.5THz is shown. Coherent detection of of the radiation from BWO and quantum cascade laser (QCL) by using unbiased SL planar diodes with supplementary low frequency (10-200GHz) pump source is demonstrated. The power spectrum of output signal frequency multiplier with the input pump of 140-160GHz is measured in frequency range 0.4-8.1THz.

articleTitle: Millimeter waves reflector with Lüneburg lenses
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this paper, a Lüneburg lens is characterized with millimeter waves. This gradient index lens is used in both transmission and reflection configurations.

articleTitle: Terahertz characterization of graphene thin films on both sides of substrate
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Graphene thin films on two sides of quartz substrate are characterized via Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy in this paper. The quartz substrate permittivity is first characterized. The graphene film is then treated as a surface boundary condition between the substrate and air. Using the uniform field approximation, the surface conductivities of graphene films are extracted. Compared to some previous approach, more accurate results in wider frequency range is achieved because of the second layer of graphene film and small substrate loss.

articleTitle: Highly birefringent liquid crystal at THz frequencies
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a liquid crystal mixture with record birefringence at THz frequencies. The mixture is characterized using a standard THz-TDS system. The birefringence exceeds 0.35. Since the mixture simultaneously shows low absorption it is ideally suited for device applications.

articleTitle: Use of plasmonic gratings for enhancing the quantum efficiency of photoconductive terahertz sources
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Using plasmonic gratings, we have greatly increased the photo-absorbing active area of a photoconductive terahertz emitter, without sacrificing device ultrafast operation. More than 20 times radiation power enhancement was measured when compared to a similar emitter without plasmonic gratings.

articleTitle: Milliwatt level output power generated by photomixing in a GaAs photoconductor
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: It is shown that a continuous wave output power of 0.35 mW at 305 GHz can be generated by photomixing in a low temperature grown GaAs photoconductor using a metallic mirror Fabry-Pérot cavity. The output power is improved by a factor of about 100 as compared to the previous works on GaAs photomixers.

articleTitle: Convolution constrained based broadband circular antenna array
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Broadband circular antenna array with convolution constrains is addressed in this paper. The circular array processor is able to scan a beam azimuthally through 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> with little change in either the beamwidth or the sidelobe level. The simulation result shows that the proposed processor steer the main beam at any arbitrary direction without using presteering delays and it has capability to cancel directional interferences as well.

articleTitle: Fiber-coupled terahertz TDS combining high speed operation with superior dynamic range
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Highly efficient mesa-structured 1.5 μm photoconductive antennas, direct detection without lock-in amplifier, and a voice-coil mirror drive with accurate position sensor are merged to a fast and precise system. A pulse trace of 25 ps is measured every 50 ms, and integration over 15 s results in a superior 75 dB dynamic range and a bandwidth of 5 THz.

articleTitle: Confidence of waveguide VNA Measurement in the frequency range of W-band and D-band
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In the frequency range of W-band and D-band, we report, in this paper, technique of evaluating typical errors which are essential factors for confidence of VNA measurements. They were estimated using the S-parameter standard developed at NMIJ. This process ensures the SI traceability in VNA measurements.

articleTitle: THz atmospheric transmission measured at antarctic Dome A
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: China is planing to construct a 5-m THz telescope (DATE5) at Dome A, Antarctic, which is the best site on the earth for astronomical observations in the THz regime. To evaluate the atmospheric transmission at Dome A, we have developed a broadband Fourier transformer spectrometer for 0.75~15 THz (Dome A FTS). The details of the instrument and measurement results will be presented.

articleTitle: Development of a passive stand-off imager using MKID technology for security and biomedical applications
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: MKIDs are cryogenic (<;1K) detectors suitable for a broad range of wavelengths and combine a high sensitivity with an intrinsic high-multiplexing capability. We plan to use the knowledge acquired in the development of MKIDs to develop a passive stand-off terahertz imager for specialized security and biomedical applications. The imager will comprise of several subcomponents, such as the focal-plane detector array unit, cryostat, warm and cold optics. A mechanical design of a scanner and re-imager optics was developed and the first images, including those of biological subjects with a prototype imager using MKIDs haven been made.

articleTitle: High TCR of VOx thin films fabricated by metal-organic decomposition for bolometer detectors
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> thin films were fabricated on fused quartz substrates by metal-organic decomposition. In R-T characteristics, VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> films indicated an abrupt phase transition around 52°C with a resistivity change of 3-4 orders and temperature coefficient of resistance of 4.4-4.8 %/K at 300 K.

articleTitle: 3-D broadband terahertz synthetic aperture imaging
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: 3-D imaging at terahertz (THz) frequencies provides a capability for a number of applications, such as explosives detection and non-destructive evaluation. Many current 3-D techniques require mechanical scanning, and often lack spectral resolution required for chemical detection. In this paper, 3-D broadband synthetic aperture imaging techniques are demonstrated by imaging familiar objects with a 2-D planar synthetic array of THz sensors.

articleTitle: A novel optical-mechanical scanning passive THz imaging system
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A novel passive THz imaging system of single channel and optical-mechanical scanning is described. It employs a Cassegrain antenna of 390mm in diameter, and achieves the two-dimensional scanning imaging via the cooperation of a line scanning mirror, driven by a crank-rocker mechanism in a high speed, and the motion of the frame scanning mirror. Thus, the system has many advantages such as low cost, simple structure, efficient and so on. The single frame imaging time of the system is only 20s, the field of view (FOV) is 30°× 36°, and the angle resolution is up to 0.6°. The experimental results show that the system can image the human body, and effectively detect dangerous items concealed under the clothes. For the images, processed by a sparse representation-based image denoising and inpainting algorithm, which generalizing the K-Means clustering process, for adapting dictionaries in order to achieve sparse signal representations. The processed image quality is improved obviously. The experimental results demonstrate, better RMSE and highest Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) compared with traditional methods can be obtained.

articleTitle: Laser-based waveform metrology at PTB: Development of an ultrabroadband voltage pulse standard
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We describe the development of a voltage pulse standard on a coplanar waveguide using laser-based optoelectronic techniques. The pulse standard, whose temporal shape (or complex frequency spectrum) is exactly known, has frequency components exceeding 500 GHz and a 500 MHz frequency spacing.

articleTitle: No genotoxic effects but mitotic disturbances found after in vitro THz field exposition of cells
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In a project funded by the German Federal Office for Radiation Protection (BfS) two different human skin cell types (HaCaT and HDF) have been exposed under defined environmental conditions to continuous-wave THz radiation at three distinct frequencies of 106 GHz, 380 GHz and 2.52 THz with free-space power densities between 0.03 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 1.96 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> adjusted traceable to the SI units. In three independent exposition campaigns no genotoxic effects have been found in the micronucleus test and in the comet assay, which have been used as end points. However, accompanying experiments on the production of mitotic disturbances in A<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> cells, a human-hamster hybrid cell line, showed that THz radiation at 106 GHz is a spindle-acting agent.

articleTitle: High performance stereolithographed W-band waveguide components for large format array instruments
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Metal-coated polymers shaped by 3D stereolithography are introduced as a new manufacturing method for passive components for millimeter to terahertz electromagnetic waves. This concept offers increased design capabilities and flexibilities while shortening the manufacturing process of complex shapes. Tests in the W-band are reported.

articleTitle: THz radiometry traceable to SI and suitable detectors
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: PTB, the metrology institute of Germany, operates the worldwide first and still unique THz detector calibration facility traceable to International System of Units. A research and development project in cooperation with a manufacturer of pyroelectric detectors is dedicated to develop suitable THz detectors.

articleTitle: Dual frequency gyrotron development for JT-60SA
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A new dual frequency (110 GHz and 138 GHz) gyrotron development began for JT-60SA. An output power and efficiency higher than 1 MW and 30% with a peak heat load lower than 1.4 kW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> were obtained for both frequencies in calculation. High mode conversion efficiencies of the quasi-optical mode converter (96.8% for 110GHz and 98.3% for 138GHz), which is higher than the previously developed 110 GHz long pulse gyrotron (96.5%), was obtained. The new gyrotron was fabricated and operation started from the middle of June 2012.

articleTitle: Geometry optimization of THz sub-harmonic Schottky mixer diodes
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a systematic analysis of geometry-dependent parasitics for THz sub-harmonic Schottky mixer diodes. In particular, the diode RF power coupling bandwidth has been studied, showing a trade-off between the air-bridge finger length and finger separation for operating frequencies beyond 1 THz.

articleTitle: The guidance for bowtie antennas design in near-field enhancement applications
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We take advantage of the 3D finite difference time domain method to systematically investigate the metallic periodic bowtie antennas. The dipoles oscillating picture is proposed to demonstrate the great enhancement of localized near-field, as well as the resonant intensities variations and dips shift.

articleTitle: Nondestructive sample preparation of pharmaceutical samples for wide frequency range THz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Sample preparation of pharmaceuticals for THz spectroscopy has much importance, as the THz spectra are often highly sensitive to crystal and/or molecular structure changes. In this study, nondestructive sample preparations will be proposed and examined.

articleTitle: 3D-Terahertz Tomography using a more realistic beam propagation model applied to different image reconstruction methods
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this paper, a model of the beam propagation is developed according to the physical properties of THz waves used in THz computed tomography (CT) scan imaging. This model is first included in an acquisition simulator to observe and estimate the impact of the Gaussian beam intensity profile on the projection sets. Second, the model is introduced in several inversion methods as a convolution filter to perform efficient tomographic reconstructions of simulated and real acquired objects. Results obtained with three reconstruction methods (BFP, SART and OSEM) are compared to the techniques proposed in this paper. We will demonstrate an increase of the overall quality and accuracy of the 3D reconstructions.

articleTitle: Extrinsic photoconductivity at 1550 nm and 1030 nm for THz Generation
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Pulses from a 1550 and 1030 nm fiber-mode-locked laser are used to drive an ErAs:GaAs photoconductive switch, resulting in extrinsic photoconductivity and useful levels of THz (~100 μW) with the 1550-nm laser drive, but not with the 1030-nm laser. This finding supports the recent discovery that extrinsic photoconductivity is a useful mechanism in ErAs:GaAs, but the THz generation is sensitive to the specific laser drive wavelength.

articleTitle: Continuous-wave coherent homodyne detection with balanced electro-optical phase modulation
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a continuous-wave coherent homodyne detection system based on terahertz (THz) phase control using balanced electro-optic phase modulation for high dynamic range. Phase-sensitive and fast THz measurement is demonstrated with a dynamic range of over 55 dB in 1-ms integration time.

articleTitle: Sub-terahertz quasi-optical reflectometer for CFRP surface inspection
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Quasioptical reflectometer based on hollow dielectric beamguide (HDB), terahertz beamguide components and elements has been developed. The reflectometer has been analyzed in terms of its application for nondestructive method for surface and subsurface contamination of carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP). Sub-terahertz (0.1...0.2 THz) measurement results of CFRP samples with different surface contaminations are presented.

articleTitle: High-power operation of terahertz oscillators with resonant tunneling diodes using offset-fed slot antennas and array configuration
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: The high-power operation of terahertz oscillators with resonant tunneling diodes using offset-fed slot antennas and an array configuration was demonstrated. A single peak was observed in the oscillation spectrum of a two-element array by mutual injection locking. Combined output powers of 610, 270, and 180 μW were obtained at 620, 770, and 810 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Determination of relaxation time of DNA hydration water by THz-TDS
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Interaction of DNA and hydration water affects both structure and function of DNA. Here, we find out the relaxation time of DNA hydration water probed by THz-TDS under biological condition. Double Debye relaxation model is applied for figuring out relaxation time of hydration water. We observed 14.9ps for 50mM of DNA solution. This is much slower compared to bulk water, 8.15ps. The results indicate the existence of slow hydration water around DNA.

articleTitle: Study of range refocusing techniques for a Terahertz Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this contribution we compare two different techniques to perform a range refocusing from 12.5 m to 37.5 m in a Terahertz Imaging Radar. The first technique, already verified experimentally, consists on the mechanical translation of the transceiver, whereas the second technique consists on the deformation of a membrane mirror with the potential to achieve larger refocusing speeds.

articleTitle: Design of resonant cavity and beam wave interaction system for a W-band sheet beam Klystron
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this paper, the dumbbell resonant cavity frequency tuning method and beam wave interaction system of W band sheet beam Klystron (WSBK) has been studied. Under the designed value of beam voltage 75kV, beam current 3.8A, and beam size of 10*0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the structures and high frequency parameters of single gap and multi-gap cavities are tested and discussed to achieve the higher output power in detail. With the tuning system proposed, the bandwidth of 100MHz can be obtained. Then, the output power is calculated by both 2-dimensional software SBK2D and the 3D PIC program, and the results agree very well.

articleTitle: Asymmetric dual-grating gate InGaAs/InAlAs/InP HEMTs for ultrafast and ultrahigh sensitive terahertz detection
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report terahertz detectors with a record sensitivity of 6.4 kV/W and noise equivalent power of 15 pW/√Hz in the above 1 THz region. The key point of this major breakthrough is careful design and fabrication of Plasmonic devices based on Field Effect Transistor structures combining interdigitated metal gates and an asymmetric metallization scheme.

articleTitle: Terahertz response of metamaterials constructed of TiO2 spheres and a metal-mesh
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We propose a simple way to construct metamaterials with negative refractive index in the terahertz region. The metamaterials composed of dielectric spheres are periodically arranged on a metal-mesh. The transmission spectra show characteristic dispersions peaked at the frequency of the Mie resonance. The combination of the negative permeability of the Mie resonance and the negative permittivity of the metal-mesh is considered to bring about this peak.

articleTitle: Terahertz thin film and refractive index sensing with a metamaterial near-field sensor
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a metamaterial-based sensor for use at terahertz (THz) frequencies that is suitable for the measurement of the thickness and the refractive index of a dielectric sample material. The sensor is designed to operate in reflection geometry in the frequency range between 1 THz and 1.6 THz. Deep-subwavelength sample thicknesses as small as 1/16000 of the operating wavelength can be resolved as well as refractive index differences of 0.01.

articleTitle: Terahertz lasing from silicon doped with boron
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Stimulated emission in the terahertz frequency range has been realized on intracenter impurity transitions of boron acceptors embedded in monocrystalline silicon under mid-infrared optical pumping at low lattice temperature. This is the first time that laser action from p-type silicon has been obtained.

articleTitle: Using THz frequency combs generated from unstabilized femtosecond lasers for near- and far-field characterization of GHz and THz emitters
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report spatially resolved measurements of frequency, phase, and amplitude of GHz and THz emitters employing an unstabilized THz frequency comb. Different detection methods are compared regarding accuracy and invasiveness.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave cameras for tokamak plasma imaging
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This paper reviews the development of millimeter-wave cameras in the 50~250 GHz region for use in plasma diagnostics on fusion plasma devices.

articleTitle: Further theoretical analysis of absorption peaks of perylene-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic dianhydride in the terahertz region
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Density functional theory calculations of its crystal elucidated that the absorption peaks of perylene 3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic dianhydride in the THz region are caused by the frequency shift and the peak splitting of the in-phase and out-of-phase vibrations of two molecules in a crystal unit cell. Crystal-packing interactions are found to enable IR-inactive vibration in isolated molecules to become IR-active vibration along with frequency shift and absorption peak splittings.

articleTitle: Development of THz bandwidth manipulation at a quasi-phase-matching device
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report on the method that terahertz generation and detection were simultaneously performed via non-collinear optical parametric interaction in a nonlinear crystals using a Si-photodiode. The bandwidth manipulation between broad 3.3 THz and narrow 45GHz bandwidths was demonstrated at single quasi-phase-matching crystal using the position-dependence of the crystal.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical conductance of a gapped graphene p-n junction in THz regime
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have carried out a theoretical and computation study of optical response of a gapped single layer graphene p-n junction in terahertz regime. It is shown that negative connectivity of single layer graphene with a gap can be important to application of graphene in coherent terahertz radiation sources and optoelectronics devices.

articleTitle: Terafly: A THz image-processing-based architecture for semi-automatic industrial inspection and measurement
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This work describes the research activity in the Terafly project which aims at the development of an automated architecture for the inspection and measurement of industrial components. The project addresses flaw detection and analysis of para-aramid synthetic fiber components by means of Terahertz 3D tomographies and CAD models. This paper describes the stages of the system, from the model-to-object mapping to the automatic geometrical measurements.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurement for CW-THz wave using a fs pulse fiber laser and a photoconductive antenna
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have started to establish an accurate frequency standard in THz region. At first an absolute frequency measurement system using a femtosecond fiber laser and a photoconductive antenna has been demonstrated for CW-THz wave. In a measurement of a 300GHz wave, we have confirmed that the measurement system has a fractional instability at the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup> level at averaging time of over 1000 seconds, corresponding to a frequency resolution of 30μHz.

articleTitle: Welcome to IRMMW-THz 2012
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Welcome to the 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter and Terahertz Waves, IRMMW-THz 2012, which is being held at the University of Wollongong, Australia.

IEEE Keywords: IEEE Microwave Theory and Techniques Society

articleTitle: Robust partitioned broadband antenna array using convolution constraints
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: This paper presents a set of constraints referred to as convolution constraints for the auxiliary beams and evaluates the performance of the partitioned processor to show that the processor with the proposed design is computationally efficient and robust against steering angle errors. The processor do not use a pre-steered array and allow an array designer to specify the frequency response in the look direction and steered the main beam in any arbitrary direction.

articleTitle: Study of ZnO nanorod and nanotube by Terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this paper we will discuss ZnO nanotube formation by chemical wet etching of ZnO nanorod. Photoluminescence measurements and Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) [1] are conducted to study its variation of optical properties. The mechanism of nanotube formation is characterized and optical properties are compared between nanorods and nanotubes.

articleTitle: A THz-frequency selective invisibility space using inhomogeneous artificial dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We theoretically and experimentally demonstrate a THz-frequency selective invisibility space using inhomogeneous artificial dielectrics. Here, a selected THz beam is made to loop around an object (larger than 5λ) that is situated on axis, effectively rendering the object invisible to the beam.

articleTitle: DAST/SiO2 multilayer structure for efficient generation of 6 THz quasi-single-cycle pulses via cascaded optical rectification
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We propose a new technique for efficient generation of 6 THz near-single-cycle transients though optical rectification of 800 nm fs laser pulses in a DAST/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> multilayer structure. The use of such a composite material allows to obtain phase-matching and control cascaded nonlinear processes.

articleTitle: Environment induced variation in the photoconductivity of graphene observed by terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Chemical vapour deposition (CVD) grown graphene sheets were investigated using optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy, revealing a dramatic variation in the photoinduced terahertz conductivity of graphene in different atmospheres.

articleTitle: Laser-excited radiation from a thin wire
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We report electromagnetic radiation covering a spectral range between radio and THz frequencies from a thin metal wire excited by ns, ps, and fs laser pulses. The transient current induced by the pondermotive force of the laser and photoemission from the wire is responsible for the radiation from the thin wire.

articleTitle: Terahertz near-field imaging of embedded metallic gratings
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We present a THz scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscope (THz s-SNOM) system. To estimate pure material resolution of our THz s-SNOM system, near-field images were obtained for embedded metallic grating. The pure material resolution of our THz s-SNOM system was estimated to be less than 100 nm.

articleTitle: A highly oversized perturbed-wall TE02 gyrotron external launcher
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A perturbed-wall TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> gyrotron external launcher with an oversize factor of 2.49 is designed using the Iterative Stratton-Chu algorithm and a Katsenelenbaum-Semenov based phase-correcting mirror design method. Radiation patterns from Surf3d show good results.

articleTitle: Phase-locking a THz quantum cascade laser to a THz comb through an all-optical beating
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate the phase-locking of a 2.5 THz Quantum Cascade Laser (QCL) to an air-propagating, 6 octaves-spanning, THz Optical Frequency Comb Synthesizer (OFCS). We directly observe the beating signal using a commercial detector, therefore proving that this approach provides a mature metrological tool in the THz region. We show that only a small fraction (<;100 nW) of the radiation emitted from the QCL is sufficient to generate a beat-note suitable for the phase-lock to the comb. These results pave the way to metrological-grade THz applications, especially in view of QCLs operating at higher temperatures.

articleTitle: Generation and detection of ultrabroadband coherent infrared pulse with 200 THz bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We generated an ultrabroadband coherent infrared pulse with 1-200 THz spectral range through an air plasma induced by a hollow-fiber compressed 10-fs, 300-μJ pulse and its second harmonic. Also we coherently detected the infrared pulse up to 100 THz with electro-optic sampling using a 20-μm thick GaSe crystal, proving that the infrared pulse was phase locked.

articleTitle: Fast terahertz imaging with a quantum-cascade laser and a scanning mirror
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A terahertz imaging system based on a quantum-cascade laser, a fast scanning mirror, and a Ge:Ga detector is demonstrated. Transmission images are obtained by scanning the beam of the quantum-cascade laser across an object. Images with a diameter of approximately 45 mm and a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 25 dB were obtained within 1.1 s. The system was also used to obtain three-dimensional images by computed tomography within an acquisition time of 87 s.

articleTitle: Nanowire and graphene architectures for Room Temperature THz detection
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: Antenna-coupled field effect transistors have been developed as plasma-wave THz detectors in both InAs nanowire and graphene channel material. Room temperature operation has been achieved up to frequencies of 1.5 THz, with noise equivalent powers as low as a few 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-11</sup> W/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>, and high-speed response.

articleTitle: The difference between oxygen and sulfur adsorption on the InSb (110) surface
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: In this paper, we compared the difference between oxygen and sulfur adsorption on the InSb (110) surface by using first-principle calculations. The theoretical calculation results have demonstrated the advantages of sulfur adsorption, which provides a reasonable way for explaining the reason of selecting sulfur passivation on the InSb surface in technology.

articleTitle: THz tomography of photo-induced carrier based on pump-probe spectroscopy in counter-propagation geometry
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have proposed a novel technique for the THz tomography of photo-induced carriers based on optical-pump THz-probe reflection spectroscopy with the counter-propagated pump and probe pulses. We have experimentally demonstrated it with silicon. The obtained complex reflection can be reproduced by the exact solution of Maxwell's equations.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave apertureless near-field microscopy using a knife blade as a scanning probe
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: A novel type of apertureless near-field microscopy using a knife blade as a scanning probe is proposed and investigated at millimeter wavelengths. Since the knife blade probe is a wider version of the metal tip probe commonly used in this technique, and therefore the interaction area between the probe tip and the sample is larger, an improvement in the intensity of the measured near-field signal, and hence in the image contrast is expected. The knife blade probe can also work as a part of a resonator in the illumination optics used in this microscopy format to enhance the strength of the near field that interacts with the sample, resulting in a further improvement in the signal intensity. A scanning method and an image reconstruction algorithm based on computerized tomography are adopted to obtain 2-D near-field images. Experiments performed at 60 GHz using a knife blade with a tip radius of 6 μm (~λ/1000) show that the signal intensity is enhanced by ~20 dB compared with an equivalent metal tip probe.

articleTitle: Analytic bandwidth expressions of travelling-wave photodetectors for broadband terahertz emitters
publicationTitle: 2012 37th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have derived analytic expressions of bandwidth limitations of travelling-wave photodetectors (TWPDs) for only-output and both input/output impedance matching cases, without any approximations. Results are effective for design of TWPD for broadband terahertz photomixer.
